question: In Faraday’s coil experiment, a galvanometer connected to a coil shows deflection only when the current in a nearby coil is switched on or switched off, but not when a steady current flows. Explain why.

options.A: Switching the nearby current on or off changes its magnetic field and hence the flux through the galvanometer coil, producing a momentary induced current. With steady current, flux is constant, so there is no deflection.
options.B: A steady current causes continuous deflection because its magnetic field is constant.
options.C: The galvanometer deflects only because the nearby coil transfers charge directly to it during switching.
options.D: The galvanometer deflects only when the nearby coil becomes permanently magnetised.
